done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. `_ran` accepts a reported node whenever the worker's name ends with `/<reported node>`. In a repo with both `app/tests/test_auth.py::test_login` and `admin/app/tests/test_auth.py::test_login`, a run of only the first test matches a proof entry for the second. Because the second source file exists, Close publishes its unrun test as passed. The command test uses only one file at each path.
findings.title: Close credits a different nested test file as passed

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Functional. A valid parameter ID such as `test_role[staff active]` appears with that space in pytest's short summary. The `\S+` match captures only `test_role[staff`, so Close cannot match the case and publishes `not run` even though it ran. The new command test covers a comma in an ID but no whitespace.
findings.title: Close loses results for pytest parameter IDs containing spaces

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
